children: By Bharath Rajeswaran

Indian shares inched higher on Friday, as lower oil prices and bargain buying after recent losses outweighed a drop in IT companies and Tata Group firms, while strong demand for domestic IPOs sucked out liquidity from secondary markets, capping gains.
The Nifty 50
rose 0.14% to 23,302.40, while the BSE Sensex
added 0.13% to 74,415.50, as of 10:33 a.m. IST.
Fifteen of the 16 major sectors advanced. The broader small-caps
and mid-caps
gained 0.9% and 0.4%, respectively.
Most Tata Group stocks fell, with TCS
, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles
, Tata Investment
, and Tata Chemicals
falling 2.5% to 8.5%.

They had advanced in the previous session after Tata Sons reappointed N. Chandrasekaran as chairman and said it would consider a public listing, while shareholder Shapoorji Pallonji Group proposed selling part of its stake.
Brent crude

fell 1.3% to $103.5 a barrel as hopes that alternative routes could keep Middle Eastern barrels flowing to global markets outweighed concerns over renewed strikes between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi movement.
Five Indian IPOs are currently open for subscription, including the National Stock Exchange of India's issue, which was subscribed 0.50 times, as of 10:30 a.m. IST.

"Crude above $100 and the IPO liquidity drain are likely to keep markets range-bound in the near term, though five weeks of declines could trigger bouts of selective bargain hunting and short covering," said Avinash Gorakshakar, founder and head of research at Avinash Mentor Research.
The Nifty IT index
fell 1.4%, with all 10 constituents in the red.
"For IT, prolonged U.S. monetary tightness and the market's preference for AI pure plays remain key overhangs, despite attractive valuations," Gorakshakar said.
Among stocks, Paytm
gained 1.2% after JPMorgan upgraded to "Overweight" from "Neutral".
Global Health
climbed 4% after Investec initiated coverage with "Buy".
Dr. Reddy's
gained 2% after signing a distribution deal with Japanese drugmaker Takeda for a dengue vaccine in India.
